claim: RDS Protection analyzes and profiles RDS login and data activity for potential threats. Login activity monitoring covers Amazon Aurora (MySQL-Compatible and PostgreSQL-Compatible), RDS for PostgreSQL, RDS for MySQL and RDS for MariaDB; data activity analysis covers Aurora PostgreSQL and RDS for PostgreSQL. It needs no additional infrastructure and is designed not to affect database performance.

evidence.quote: RDS Protection doesn't require additional infrastructure; it is designed so as not to affect the performance of your database instances.
RDS Protection in Amazon GuardDuty analyzes and profiles RDS login and data activity for potential threats to your Amazon Aurora and RDS for PostgreSQL databases.

RDS Protection for login activity analyzes login events for potential access threats to [Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html) (Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition and Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition), [RDS for PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_PostgreSQL.html), [Amazon RDS for MySQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MySQL.html), and [Amazon RDS for MariaDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MariaDB.html) databases.

RDS Protection for data activity analyzes database query patterns on [Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html) for PostgreSQL and [RDS for PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_PostgreSQL.html) databases to detect potential data access and manipulation threats.
